text.title: Activation Metrics Failure Modes
text.summary: Six antipatterns observed when applying Activation Metrics. Each pairs symptom + root-cause + concrete fix. Detector clauses make them mechanically catchable.

antipattern.symptom: Activation rate in the report is far above the rate the finance or product team computes from signups; the two numbers never reconcile.
antipattern.root-cause: Denominator silently switched to "users who reached step 2" or "verified emails".
antipattern.fix: Recompute against all signups per `r-activation-rate-denominator-is-signups`; if a narrowed rate is useful, add it as a separately named metric.

antipattern.symptom: The most recent week always shows a sharp activation drop that disappears the following week.
antipattern.root-cause: Cohorts whose window has not elapsed included in the rate.
antipattern.fix: Exclude or mark `_partial` per `r-one-fixed-window-closed-cohorts-only`; set `period_end` to the last closed cohort.

antipattern.symptom: Aggregate activation falls 5pp in a week where onboarding did not change; a paid campaign launched the same week.
antipattern.root-cause: Only the blended rate reported; no per-channel breakdown.
antipattern.fix: Add `activation_rate__<channel>` metrics per `r-segment-by-acquisition-channel` and state the mix shift in the finding.

antipattern.symptom: Time-to-activation reported as a single mean of several days while session data shows most users activate within the first session.

root-cause.source: widely established statistics practice for skewed durations

antipattern.root-cause: Right-skewed distribution summarised by its mean.

antipattern.symptom: Finding says "users who invite a teammate retain 3x better" with no group sizes and no cohort age; the cohort is 12 days old.
antipattern.root-cause: Lift table built from a projection and read as a causal effect.
antipattern.fix: Rebuild on a cohort at least 30 days old with both rates and sizes per `r-d30-lift-table-with-sizes`; reword as correlation.

antipattern.symptom: `metrics[]` contains `"value": 31` and `"value": 0.31` for the same metric across two weeks; the WoW delta is computed as a 30pp jump.
antipattern.root-cause: No unit convention; rate typed once as percent and once as ratio.
antipattern.fix: Enforce `r-metric-naming-and-units`: ratios 0-1, deltas in `pp`, unit present on every entry.
